video.title: I Tested How Passive This AI Side Hustle Really Is

summary: Chris Koerner connects Claude to Omnisend and uses AI agents to send a paid consulting offer to people on his email list. The one week experiment reports $80 from 1,013 emails, with 16 calls estimated to take 80 minutes. Koerner says the $5 price, an unclear free email reply path, and the lack of follow-up weakened the campaign, and he considers testing a much higher hourly price. The tools automate campaign setup and analysis, but the consulting itself still depends on his time; Omnisend is also a promotional partner.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; runs the consulting email experiment.

ideas.name: Five-minute business consulting
ideas.one_liner: Sell short business advice sessions to people on an existing email list, with potential coaching and higher-ticket upsells.
ideas.business_model: One-off paid consultation, with possible upsells to coaching packages, recurring services, higher-ticket work, or AI audits.
ideas.customer: People in Koerner's network who like business ideas or own businesses and may have business questions.
ideas.problem: Customers want a quick answer about a business problem, idea, or next move.
ideas.offer: A five-minute live consultation booked through TidyCal for $5, with an email-reply option also offered. Koerner mentions coaching packages, recurring work, higher-ticket work, and AI audits as possible upsells.

pricing.model: Per booking for a short consultation; possible upsells are not priced.

price_points.label: Equivalent implied by the $5 five-minute session
Equivalent implied by the $5 five-minute session
Proposed future price test; not tested in this video

pricing.notes: The email also offered replies as a way to ask questions, which some recipients understood as free. Coaching, recurring services, and AI audits were mentioned as possible upsells without prices.

acquisition_channels.details: Koerner selected contacts from his network and emailed his audience through Omnisend. The video later describes 1,013 campaign emails and discusses sending to his full list.

quote.text: Well, these are people in my network that I'm going to email, but I want to randomize them, because I'm only going to email a set limited number of people
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Koerner personally delivers the five-minute live consultations and may answer questions by email. TidyCal takes bookings, Stripe handles payment, and the booking calendar syncs with his calendar.
unit_economics_claims: Koerner reports $80 in campaign revenue from 16 calls, and estimates 80 minutes of consultation time.
He calculates campaign revenue per recipient at about $0.08.
He claims he has no costs, but does not quantify payment processing or software fees.
His $120,000-per-year illustration assumes 40 paid hours per week at $60 per hour; it is hypothetical, not observed profit.
He says a $1,000-per-hour consultation could yield 12 times the revenue from the same email send, but this was only a proposed test.
ideas.startup_cost: Koerner says he has no costs for selling his time. Actual payment-processing and software costs are not stated.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. Koerner reviewed campaign results one week after sending the email.

acquisition.how: Claude and Omnisend can segment contacts, draft, and send campaigns. Building a permission-based audience and choosing the offer still need human direction and review.

onboarding.how: TidyCal, Stripe, and calendar syncing can take payment and book an available slot automatically, subject to occasional checks.

delivery.how: Koerner must personally conduct each live consultation or write each substantive email answer.

billing.how: Stripe is integrated into the booking flow and can collect the stated booking price automatically; exceptions and accounting still need review.

support.how: Questions and consulting answers require Koerner's judgement and time. Agents could draft routine replies, but the paid advice remains human-led.

uk_applicability.notes: The consulting and booking model can work in the UK, but email acquisition needs UK PECR compliance: obtain consent for marketing to individuals and sole traders unless an exception applies; marketing to corporate subscribers has different rules. Cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS. Adapt the currency and payment terms for UK customers.

risks: The $5 price may signal low quality and earns little for each human-delivered session.
Offering a reply-by-email path alongside a paid booking confused some recipients about whether advice was free.
The reported campaign revenue does not establish that the same response rates will hold across the full list or at a much higher price.
The business sells Koerner's time, so it does not run almost entirely on agents.
In the UK, sending marketing emails to individuals or sole traders without the required consent can breach PECR.
Koerner granted the AI connector read and write access to Omnisend, creating account and data risks if access is misconfigured.

tactics.name: Randomize a small initial audience
steps: Put the candidate email contacts into Google Sheets.
Use the RAND formula to assign a random number to each row.
Sort by the random number and select a limited group for the initial campaign.
Export the selected contacts as a CSV.

quote.text: So, I'm going to use this formula in Google Sheets, equals rand open parentheses close parentheses, that assigns a perfectly randomized number to that row.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Connect an AI agent to the email platform
steps: Add Omnisend as a custom connector in Claude using the MCP URL shown in the video.
Authorize the connection and import the selected CSV into an Omnisend segment.
Ask Claude to draft the email and create or send the campaign through the connector.
Review permission requests and campaign content before allowing actions.

quote.text: This removes the need for me to log in to Omnisend at all, and I can still use it and enjoy all the features of it.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Create a paid short-consult booking link
steps: Set up a five-minute TidyCal booking page.
Connect Stripe and charge $5 per booking.
Sync the link to the calendar to avoid double-booking.
Limit the available times to selected weekdays and hours.

quote.text: Duration of the meeting is 5 minutes. We're going to go to pricing. Charge $5 per booking. I integrated Stripe just with a couple clicks.

tactics.name: Keep the initial campaign plain and direct
steps: Send a plain-text email with one clear booking link.
Use a short subject line; Koerner chose "$5".
Check that the booking link works before sending.
Make the payment requirement and the paid route explicit so email replies are not mistaken for free advice.

quote.text: I just want this to be plain text, one link for them to click on where they can buy, and I'm going to tell it what subject line to use.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Review campaign results with connected data
steps: Ask Claude to summarize the Omnisend campaign.
Connect Stripe data so the agent can compare clicks, buyers, and revenue.
Review sends, delivery, opens, clicks, replies, bookings, and revenue before deciding on a follow-up.

quote.text: So, I also have Stripe connected through my Claude MCP, so it was able to cross-reference the clicks to the buyers and Stripe and put everything all in one chart.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Follow up with interested prospects
steps: Do not stop after the first email; send relevant follow-ups to people who may still be deciding.
Use the children's market example as a reminder that another vendor email led to four additional sign-ups.

tactics.name: Improve the next email using observed weaknesses
steps: Add a reason to act now if one genuinely exists.
Use one clear paid path rather than mixing a paid booking link with a reply path that appears free.
Add relevant proof and make the offer more specific.
Use a clear, descriptive booking link and follow up.
Ask Claude to create drafts in the email platform, then review them before sending.

steps: Compare the low-priced five-minute offer with a proposed $1,000 one-hour consultation.

warnings.warning: Koerner says Omnisend would not send until he had a verified sender. Email marketing requires proper sender verification and applicable legal compliance.

quote.text: Okay, so it said, "Hey, I can't send this until there's a verified sender." That is a regulation, it's not Omnisend's choice.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Koerner granted the connector broad read and write permissions. That creates a risk if the AI account, connector, or data access is compromised or misused.

quote.text: I'm going to give it all read and write permissions, because I'm trusting like that
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The email's reply-by-email option confused recipients about whether they could get an answer for free, weakening the paid booking path.

quote.text: The free path ate the paid path. I guess it was confusing. Some people thought they could just reply to the email and get an answer for free
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Koerner says the $5 price could make the offer seem like a joke or low quality.

quote.text: And $5 signals junk. That's exactly what I just said about pricing. It sounds like a gag.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Koerner says the campaign lacked proof, testimonials, specificity, and follow-up, so the reported one-campaign results should not be treated as validated repeatable performance.

quote.text: No proof, no testimonials, no reviews, no specificity. Booking link is a naked URL. And I never followed up
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: In the UK, marketing emails to individuals and sole traders generally need consent unless an applicable exception applies; cold calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS.
The campaign's reported response rates come from one email send; extrapolating them to a full list or a different price is not evidence that the projection will hold.

quote.text: If I were to send this to my entire list and these percentages carried through, then it would be a six-figure consulting business at a ridiculously low rate.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A person can sell practical knowledge without a degree or impressive credentials if they find customers who want that knowledge.

quote.text: You don't need a college degree, you don't need a ton of accolades, or an impressive resume to charge for your services.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Price affects perceived quality as well as revenue; a very low price can make an offer seem less credible.

quote.text: But, if it's three bucks, it's like, "Yeah, that's what a hot dog should cost." If it's 10 bucks, it's like,
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Make the paid route unambiguous. A free-looking reply option can divert customers from a paid booking.

quote.text: The free path ate the paid path. I guess it was confusing. Some people thought they could just reply to the email and get an answer for free
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Follow-up can produce additional sign-ups, but marketing follow-ups must respect recipients' consent and preferences.

quote.text: And what do you know? She sent another email, and she got four more sign-ups for the kids market.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: An MCP connection lets an AI agent carry out work inside another service, including importing contacts and drafting campaign emails.

quote.text: You can run your entire account from inside ChatGPT or Claude. You can understand your performance, build segments, read to it, write to it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Automating campaign operations does not automate the human expertise being sold; Koerner still has to deliver each consultation.

quote.text: So, I'm going to make from these 16 calls $80, and it's going to take 80 minutes of my time, an hour and 20 minutes
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Review campaign outcomes and improve the offer, proof, call to action, timing, and follow-up rather than assuming a first send is optimized.

quote.text: Didn't do a bunch of AB tests. Didn't send it at the right time of day. So, with a little more tweaking, I could have done a bit better here.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Treat an attractive annualized calculation as a hypothesis when it depends on assumed hours, response rates, and prices.

quote.text: If I were to send this to my entire list and these percentages carried through, then it would be a six-figure consulting business at a ridiculously low rate.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Use AI to produce drafts inside the operating platform, then inspect those drafts before they are sent.

quote.text: In other words, don't just read what's in there or tell me what to paste over there. Show me what you're putting over there, and then actually create the drafts in Omnisend.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: Koerner describes a first-hand one-week campaign and reports specific email and revenue metrics, plus the setup steps. The figures are self-reported, the experiment is small, and the video does not provide independently verifiable campaign records. The claimed annual outcome is hypothetical.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Koerner says Omnisend supports the podcast and promotes its performance claims and discount code. He also recommends Beehiiv in a promotional segment.
